description: Test layers and their wall-clock budgets. Run with `node .github/eos/run-tests.mjs`. A layer is a set of files that run in ONE `node --test` invocation, so Node parallelises them across cores. budgetMs is the ABSOLUTE ceiling everywhere, calibrated against the CI runner that enforces it (about 1.8x its observed time): the first budgets were set from a 16-core laptop, so on the 2-core runner audit-regression already sat at 95%. Slow creep below the ceiling is the job of the per-environment baseline (EOS_TEST_BASELINE_ENV, baselineTolerance). On a slow runner set EOS_TEST_BUDGET_SCALE instead of raising a budget, so the ratio a breach represents stays the same everywhere. Runner speed varies as much as the drift tolerance: the same commit (2daa3e3) took 20.6s and 31.2s for integration on two ubuntu-latest runs, every file scaled alike. So the ci-linux baselines are recorded from the slower runner class (eos-2.0.0: integration grew by four suites — first run, release signing, policy upstream, governance report), and each budget stays about 1.8x of it. eos-2.2.0/2.3.0 re-recorded integration, contract and audit-regression: six integration suites were added since 2.0.0 (JUnit evidence, skills, agent platforms, brownfield, stage init, MCP stop), the MCP contract suite, and the eval-starter replay cases; the slower runner class then measured integration 52.9s, contract 16.7s, and audit-regression 38.5s at most (its audit step was skipped after the integration step failed on drift), while a fast runner took 32.4s / 11.8s / 26.4s for the same commit.

coverage.description: Thresholds for `run-tests.mjs --coverage`. Set just below the measured figure (lines 96.9 / branches 75.8 / functions 96.3 at the time of writing) so they catch a real regression rather than chasing a round number. Enforced natively by Node 22+; on Node 20 the report still prints but the threshold is not applied, and run-tests says so rather than implying it passed.

unit.description: Pure logic and single-module behaviour. No repository fixtures beyond a temp dir.

contract.description: Published interfaces: the CLI's JSON contract and exit codes, the provider-adapter contract, and the offline boundary that both rest on.

integration.description: Several modules together through real fixtures: routing decisions, gate bypasses, cross-stack quality.

journey.description: The whole developer loop end to end, executed through the real CLI, offline.

audit-regression.description: One executable case per audit finding. Each test performs the reported bypass, then asserts it no longer works. A failure here means an audit finding has re-opened.
